schema.title: Response List Runs Auto Runs Get

get.description: The plan a new Auto Run starts from for `version`: every phase on except mid-training, continue on a pass, pause on a failure.

put.description: Only a draft or paused run (else 409), and for a paused one only the current and later phases that have no job yet (else 422).

post.description: Skip the current phase (a failed, stopped, blocked or not yet started one). The run stays as it is; resume it.
The runs a Compare setup would make, and how each variant is matched to the base. Queues nothing. 422 says why a setup cannot run.
Queue the runs of a Compare setup. It needs a variant and plain text to train on.
The finished Compare runs experiments, oldest first. The result is a list of CompareRunOut.

Lettered problems answered with 0, 1 and a few worked examples in the prompt, and no training. Slow.
The result is a FewShotOut.

The benchmark track as stored, one row per trained version; never scores anything. A job: it reads the held-back data.
The result is a BenchmarkOut.
Score (or read back) the suite for one trained version. Slow. The result is the suite's dict for that version.

get.description: How much training the newer of versions `a` and `b` saved over the older; no verdict unless both finished the same schedule.
Everything busy now, oldest first. Empty when idle.

post.description: Save a correction: for round 3 (the teacher sees it, the student does not), or with `whole_answer` as a round 1 conversation.
Save a rated pair for round 4: the answer the user preferred and the one they did not.
Stream the reply as server-sent events: `text` ({text}: the reply so far), then `done` ({text}) or `error` ({message}).

get.description:
The allow lists of this node and its owner's Tailscale login. The login is what a machine that answers 401 to this one must
add to its own allow_users. The funnel token and any other key of studioConfig.cluster are never returned.

put.description:
Save the allow lists in the workspace config, keeping every other key of studioConfig.cluster. Entries are stripped and repeats
dropped. 400 with a sentence for a bad entry. The API reads the lists when it starts: a change counts after it is restarted.

get.description: Jobs queued here that run or wait to run on a peer (with the reason for a wait), and jobs this node runs for another.

post.description:
Take a job another node owns. 409 when this node cannot run it (no version store, a kind that does not leave its owner) or the
lease is older than one it holds.
A runner's job ended; the finished version is in the store. 409 for any epoch but the current one.

A runner extends its lease and reports progress; its events are re-emitted here as if the job ran here. 409 for any epoch but
the current one: the job has been placed again, and the runner must stop its copy.
The owner no longer wants this copy of the job. 409 when the epoch is not the one this node holds.

get.description:
The jobs of every machine, each with the machine it runs on or is pinned to. The peers are asked at the same time, for their
node and their queue, and answer within two seconds or not at all; a peer that does not keeps its last known rows, marked stale.
Sync, so the peers are asked off the event loop. Empty when no other machine is listed, except that a job still running on a machine
that was removed from the list keeps its row, so its note (for example, a refused checkpoint) is still said.

This node first, then every listed peer, in list order. A peer that does not answer within two seconds is listed offline with
the reason, never dropped. Sync, so the GPU probe and the peers (asked at the same time) run off the event loop. This node's
tailnet name comes from the host-name refresh (studio_api.hosts), never from a call to tailscale while the request waits.

put.description:
Save the list of other machines in the workspace config. Entries are stripped, blank and repeated ones dropped; the saved list
comes back. 400 with a sentence for an entry that is not a machine address.

post.description:
Stop, or drop, a job that another machine queued, by asking that machine (DELETE /queue/jobs/{id} there). The machine must be
one of the listed peers. A job queued here is stopped with DELETE /queue/jobs/{id} on this node. The peer's own refusal (401,
404, a timeout) comes back as 502 with its sentence.

get.description: The cluster self-test as it stands: its steps while it runs, else the last one's (kept across restarts), else state `never`.

post.description:
Start the self-test with the listed machines: the checks per machine, then a tiny real DiLoCo run through the queue, invite and
join path, each step with its verdict. 409 with a sentence when it cannot start (one is running, this computer is busy, an address is
not on the Machines list).

Download the weights of an open round from the coordinator at `url`, as a member does, and answer their checksum. 409 when the
round has closed or the coordinator refused.
Asked by the machine running the self-test: can this one reach `url` (that machine, by the address it gave its members)?

get.description: What the collector is doing now.

put.description: Save settings. 400 with a sentence for a bad value (a site that is excluded, a cap out of range). Turning collection on starts it.

get.description: Topics, sources with their licence and terms notes, the sites that are never collected.

post.description: Pause now; the collector notices within a second.
Resume, turning collection on if it was off.

Join (or re-join with a newer epoch). Takes effect at the next round boundary, at once when no round is open.
A member that does not know the term yet sends 0 and learns it from the answer.

its speed). `part` of `count` parts, the whole body `total` bytes with hash `sha256`; the part carries its own `part_sha256`.

400 when a part or the whole fails its hash: the member sends it again). `count=0` takes nothing: it asks whether this route exists.

get.description:
Every run in the cluster, newest first, each with its members and rounds and the `origin` that wrote it and its `age_s`. Runs

schema.title: Response List Runs Distributed Runs Get

post.description:
Queue a distributed pretraining run of a design on the chosen text, with this computer as coordinator and member. The chosen
machines are invited when the run starts, and the form's settings are checked here (400 with a sentence). With `all_machines`
every listed machine that answers on this app version is invited and the rest are left out (`left_out` in the job's params,
each with a reason); with `replaces` the run takes a waiting pretrain job's version, text and place in the queue, and the
pretrain job leaves the queue. With `coordinator` (one of the invited machines, which must answer on this app version: else 400
or 409 with the reason) this computer starts the run and hands the coordinator role to that machine once it holds a finished
round (studio_failover, "handoff"); without it this computer coordinates throughout.

Turn on or off inviting machines that come online while the run goes. Off: only the machines chosen, or that ask to join, are
offered a slot; a machine already invited stays. A run another computer coordinates is changed by asking that computer. 409 when the run is over.

Make a run going on longer: `rounds` is the new total (more than it has), `inner_steps` the new H for the rounds still to come
(the outer learning rate and momentum stay as they are). Every member takes the change from its next rounds without leaving, and
the learning rate carries on from where it is. 409 when the run is over or not going, 422 for numbers that change nothing or shorten
the run (Stop ends it sooner). A run another computer coordinates is extended by asking that computer.

Ask the computer that coordinates a running run to add this one: it joins from the round after its invitation. 409 for a run
this computer coordinates; the coordinator's own refusals come back as they are.

get.description:

post.description:
The coordinator's side of a join: add `node`, one of this computer's listed machines, to the running run. The scheduler offers
it a slot now and invites it, and it trains from the round after; a machine that is busy gets a slot once it is free. 409 when the
run is not running here, for a node that is not listed, already in the run, or stopped by the owner, and for a full run.

Take one member out of a run and keep it out. The others carry on from the next round. 409 for this computer (stop the run)
and for a node that is not a member. A run another computer coordinates: that computer is asked.

Hold a run: no new round opens until it is resumed. A round in flight finishes, the members wait, and the paused time does not
count toward the run's time limit. It stays paused over a restart of the app. 409 when the run is over or not going. A run
another computer coordinates is paused by asking that computer.

Start a new run (a new id) from an ended one: the same design, text, settings and machines, with the weights of the old run's
best round (else its last) as the starting point. The outer momentum starts at zero. 409 for a run that is still going, one
that saved no weights, or one this computer did not start. A run another computer coordinates is restarted by that computer.
Undo a pause: the next round opens as soon as the members are in. 409 when the run is over or not going.

End a run. Every member is told it is finished at its next call, and the member jobs leave the other machines' queues. The
weights of the last finished round stay in the run's folder. A run another computer coordinates is stopped by asking that computer.

What a start with these settings would give each machine, before it is started: the Training tab shows it beside the form.
Null when this computer cannot read its own hardware. The machines are the ones a start would invite; nothing is queued.

post.description:
Services.enqueue: add a job to the end of Up next, or answer the job already queued under the caller's `id`. An unknown kind is a
400.

delete.description:
Services.remove: drop a waiting job, or stop the running one, including one that runs on a peer (it is told to stop). On a
failed job it dismisses it from the list.

post.description: Services.hold: a held job keeps its place and is skipped; held=false releases it.
Services.move: put a waiting job at `index` in Up next (0 runs next).
Services.move_up: one place earlier in Up next.

get.description: Services.queue_outlook for a queued job: when it starts. Empty once it has left the queue.

post.description:
Keep a waiting job on one machine (`pinned`: its address or hostname), or let it go anywhere again (null). A pin is never
overridden: the job runs there or waits, and its waiting reason says why. Services has no pin, so a node with a job queue
pins through the Runner, and the stand-in services edit the job in place.

Run a failed job again: a copy with the same kind, label, note and params goes first in Up next, and the failed entry is
dismissed. Only a failed job restarts; any other id is a 404.

Run a waiting job now: release it if held, put it first in Up next, lift a pause and start the queue, answering as Start
does. A job already running is not stopped: the chosen one goes next. The plan (hours, battery, idle) still holds it.

with its sentence, instead of a bare 200 followed by a job that has quietly gone.

Queue a pretrain job that continues the version's newest run. The job's result is {job_id, label, version, kind, from_step}; the

post.description:
Upload the version's weights (half precision, no optimizer state) and metadata to the version store. The job's result is
{key, number, origin}. 409 with a sentence when no store is configured or the version has not trained.

Download a published version and add it here as a trained version (`number` is its number on the machine that published it;
`origin` says which machine when several published one). The job's result is the new version, and its progress says where the
weights came from. The machine that published it is asked first (`/weights`), when the workspace lists it among its nodes and it
answers; with `origin` given the store is not read then. Otherwise, or when it cannot send it, they come from the store. 409 when
no store is configured.
What the version's run did ({data, steps, tokens, start, lr, extra}). The first read hashes the data file.

Held-out bits per character of the version's run-in-progress checkpoint. The job's result is {version, step, saved_at, bpc,
documents}, for the caller only: nothing is stored, and the version's checkpoint, scorecard and status do not change.

them first with `/weights/meta`; the sha256 there is what the download must hash to.

machine. The first call makes the half-precision copy and may take a while. 409 when the version has not trained.
